title: Lexington, Concord & Bunker Hill
summary: The war begins: British regulars march on Concord and are harried back to Boston, then pay heavily to take the Charlestown heights.

title: Washington rides to Cambridge
summary: The new commander in chief's journey from Philadelphia through New York and New England to take command outside Boston.

title: Siege of Boston
summary: An arc of American lines from Roxbury to Charlestown Neck bottles up the British garrison on the Boston peninsula.

title: Invasion of Canada
summary: Arnold's wilderness march and Montgomery's advance converge on Quebec; the failed assault leads to a retreat ending at Valcour Island.

title: Knox's "noble train" of artillery
summary: Henry Knox hauls some sixty tons of cannon from Fort Ticonderoga across frozen lakes and the Berkshires to Cambridge.

title: Dorchester Heights & the evacuation of Boston
summary: In one night the Americans fortify the heights above the harbor with Knox's guns, forcing Howe to abandon Boston.

title: Sullivan's Island
summary: A British fleet's attack on the palmetto-log fort guarding Charleston harbor ends in a costly failure.

title: Defending New York
summary: Washington spreads his army across Manhattan, Brooklyn and the Hudson forts as the largest British fleet yet seen gathers off Staten Island.

title: Battle of Long Island & the East River retreat
summary: Howe's night march through Jamaica Pass outflanks the American line; two nights later the army escapes across the East River.

title: Kip's Bay & Harlem Heights
summary: A British landing at Kip's Bay routs the defenders and nearly traps the army in lower Manhattan; next day the Americans hold at Harlem Heights.

title: Throg's Neck to White Plains
summary: Howe lands in Westchester to get behind the army; Washington withdraws north and fights at Chatterton's Hill.

title: Fall of Fort Washington & Fort Lee
summary: The last American stronghold on Manhattan falls with nearly 3,000 men; days later Fort Lee across the Hudson is abandoned.

title: Retreat across New Jersey
summary: The dwindling army falls back from the Hackensack to the Delaware with Cornwallis close behind; Charles Lee is captured at Basking Ridge.

title: Crossing the Delaware & Trenton
summary: On Christmas night Washington crosses the icy Delaware and surprises the Hessian garrison at Trenton at dawn.

title: Assunpink Creek & Princeton
summary: Pinned against Assunpink Creek, the army slips away by night and defeats the British rear guard at Princeton.

title: Winter at Morristown
summary: Behind the Watchung hills the army winters within striking distance of the roads between New York and Philadelphia.

title: Howe sails for Philadelphia
summary: Howe's army goes by sea from New York around to the head of the Chesapeake while Washington marches south to meet him.

title: Brandywine
summary: While a Hessian force pins Washington at Chadds Ford, Howe's main column crosses upstream and strikes the American right flank.

title: Fall of Philadelphia & Germantown
summary: Maneuvers along the Schuylkill lose Philadelphia; Washington's four-column dawn attack at Germantown falters in fog.

title: Saratoga campaign
summary: Burgoyne advances from Canada down Lake Champlain toward Albany and is forced to surrender his army at Saratoga.

title: Delaware River forts & Whitemarsh
summary: Forts Mifflin and Mercer hold the river against the British fleet for weeks; Howe probes Washington's camp at Whitemarsh before winter.

title: Valley Forge
summary: The army's winter encampment on a plateau above the Schuylkill, a day's march from British-held Philadelphia.

title: Monmouth campaign
summary: Clinton evacuates Philadelphia across New Jersey; Lee's advance guard attack collapses and Washington rallies the army at Monmouth Court House.

title: Newport
summary: The first Franco-American operation against British-held Newport founders when a storm scatters d'Estaing's fleet.

title: Savannah
summary: The British take Savannah; a year later a French and American siege fails with heavy losses in a dawn assault.

title: Sullivan–Clinton expedition
summary: Washington sends an army into Iroquois country, burning towns and crops across the Finger Lakes region.

title: Stony Point & Paulus Hook
summary: Night bayonet raids retake a fortified Hudson River point and strike a British post opposite New York.

title: The hard winter at Morristown
summary: The army huts at Jockey Hollow through the harshest winter of the war; in June, Greene's Continentals and the New Jersey militia turn back a British thrust at Springfield.

title: Charleston & Camden
summary: Charleston falls with its whole garrison, Gates is routed at Camden, and the tide turns at King's Mountain.

title: Arnold's treason at West Point
summary: Arnold plots to hand over West Point; André is caught near Tarrytown, and Arnold flees to a British ship hours before Washington arrives.

title: Cowpens to Guilford Courthouse
summary: Morgan destroys Tarleton's force at Cowpens; Greene leads Cornwallis on a race to the Dan and bleeds him at Guilford Courthouse.

title: War in Virginia
summary: Arnold raids Richmond, a British sloop extorts supplies from Mount Vernon, and Cornwallis chases Lafayette before falling back to Yorktown.

title: The march to Yorktown
summary: The allied armies feint at New York, then march to the Chesapeake while two French fleets converge on Virginia.

title: Battle of the Capes
summary: De Grasse's fleet fights Graves off the Virginia Capes, sealing Cornwallis off from the sea.

title: Siege of Yorktown
summary: Allied trenches close on Cornwallis's lines; after Redoubts 9 and 10 fall, the British surrender.

title: Evacuation of New York & the road home
summary: Washington enters New York as the British sail away, bids his officers farewell, resigns his commission at Annapolis, and reaches Mount Vernon by Christmas Eve.
